newsitem.title: USA: Ross could return to Mideast talks soon.
newsitem.headline: Ross could return to Mideast talks soon.

text.p: U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross, who is returning home from inconclusive Israeli-Palestinian talks, can return to the region quickly if needed, U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher said on Monday.

"Dennis will be prepared to go back in a few days, a week or so, as soon as his presence there will once again be very useful," Christopher told reporters and his spokesman predicted the talks would ultimately succeed.

Ross said earlier at a news conference in Jerusalem that he was leaving for Washington to report to Christopher after mediating for 15 days in the talks, which centre on a partial Israel pull-back from the West Bank town of Hebron.
White House spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters that while Ross returned to consult with Christopher, the Israeli-Palestinian talks would go ahead.
"They are in a non-stop format," he added, noting that both the U.S. ambassador to Israel and the consul general in Jerusalem remained engaged in the discussions.

"We are encouraging both parties to stay at the table and to continue to address those issues (relevant) to implementing the agreements that are already reached," McCurry said during a campaign stop by President Bill Clinton in Parma, Ohio.
Christopher denied that the talks had broken down but said difficult issues still separate the negotiators.

"The progress that has been made has not been sufficient to conclude that issue because the issues are very difficult and require a good deal of precision," Christopher said before talks with Ukrainian Foreign Minister Hennady Udovenko.
"But the talks will continue, the United States role will continue" with U.S. diplomats in the region standing in for Ross, he said. "The negotiations are very detailed, very difficult."

State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said the United States thought Israel and the Palestinians had "made a lot of progress ... We think that certainly Israel and the Palestinians have a greater sense of what the end result must be."

"We're confident of success in the end. But they're tough talks, and despite all the positive predictions in the Israeli press, including this morning, that the talks are about to succeed, they've still got a ways to go," he said.
